resources.string: SIM Card Policy
Wi-Fi Rule Library
Enable policy for SIM %1$d (%2$s)
When off, no policy applies to this SIM: no network quality downgrade, no drop to 4G on Wi-Fi, and Wi-Fi rules will not switch data to this SIM.
Custom: each item has its own switch and runs only when enabled
Network quality auto-downgrade

Trigger: the default data SIM shows fake full bars but the network is bad (ping timeouts, low SINR), or the signal is weak. Action: automatically downgrade to 4G. Restore: after several consecutive good probes, the original network mode is written back.
Drop to 4G on Wi-Fi

Trigger: connected to any Wi-Fi. Action: immediately downgrade to 4G (default 4G/3G/2G auto) to save power. Restore: after you disconnect from Wi-Fi or turn this switch off, the network mode from before the connection is written back.
What the rules manage

The rules manage the default data SIM: when you connect to a Wi-Fi network listed in a rule, the default SIM switches to the SIM the rule specifies; if no target is specified, only a match is recorded and no switch happens. Whether it switches back after you leave depends on \"Revert after leaving Wi-Fi\".

Matching: if a BSSID is set, match by exact BSSID; otherwise match by SSID, case-insensitive; if both are empty, match any Wi-Fi. When several rules match, the higher priority number runs first; if they are equal, the one earlier in the list wins.

Cooldown: right after a rule switches, it will not trigger again during the cooldown, so you do not flip back and forth at the edge of Wi-Fi coverage. The cooldown only limits repeat triggers; it does not affect \"revert after leaving\".
Master switch: when off, no Wi-Fi rule matches, no SIM is switched and no network mode is changed
New rule
%1$s · Priority %2$d · Cooldown %3$d s
· Revert to the original SIM after leaving
On match, switch to: SIM %1$d
On match, switch to: no switch (just record one match)
Also set the target SIM network mode to: %1$s
Leave the target SIM network mode unchanged
Match conditions
What happens on match
Leave both SSID and BSSID empty = match any Wi-Fi; usually given a low priority as a fallback. If a BSSID is set, matching is by exact BSSID, which pins down one AP when several share the same SSID.

Choose \"Any SIM\" = no switch; a match is only recorded once and the network mode setting below has no effect. Choose a specific SIM = when you connect to that Wi-Fi, the default SIM switches to it; if the policy master switch for that SIM is off, this rule does not run.
The higher the priority number, the earlier it is picked. When several rules match at once, only the highest one runs; 0 is allowed, and if the numbers are equal the one earlier in the list wins.

Cooldown (seconds): after one switch, the rule will not trigger again for this many seconds, avoiding repeated SIM switches at the edge of Wi-Fi coverage. 0 means always allowed; the maximum is 3600 seconds.
On: after you leave the Wi-Fi matched by this rule, the default SIM automatically switches back to the original one. Off: the current SIM is kept after you leave.
